attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-09-15
Provider: Dr. Marcus Johnson, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Found unresponsive in friend's bathroom during house party with shallow respirations.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns to the emergency department eight months after a prior encounter in January 2020 when she was found unresponsive at an outdoor music festival. Her friends state that she had come over for a small house party and had been behaving normally until she went into the bathroom about an hour earlier and never came out. After knocking repeatedly, they broke down the door and found her slumped over on the floor, breathing shallowly and unresponsive. They immediately called 911. On the way to the hospital, EMS noted a respiratory rate of 6/min and administered oxygen via non-rebreather mask. Her friends deny that she was drinking or using illicit drugs, but one reports that she had recently been complaining of neck pain and may have taken "something strong" for it.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Opioid overdose (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

MEDICATIONS:
She does not take any prescription medications,

ALLERGIES:
She has no known allergies.

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Family history of substance use disorder (paternal uncle, untreated)
- Family history of major depressive disorder (mother)

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Part-time yoga instructor.

VITAL SIGNS:
Her temperature is 36.2°C (97.2°F), blood pressure is 100/60 mm Hg, pulse is 52/min, respiratory rate is 6/min, and oxygen saturation is 89% on 100% non-rebreather oxygen.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the patient is unresponsive to voice and noxious stimuli. Her pupils are 1 mm bilaterally and sluggishly reactive. Lung sounds are clear bilaterally with decreased chest excursion. Heart sounds are normal without murmur. There are no signs of trauma, needle marks, or skin changes. Her extremities are warm with no edema.

LABORATORY DATA:
Capillary glucose is 96 mg/dL. Bedside ABG shows pH 7.21, PaCO₂ 70 mm Hg, PaO₂ 60 mm Hg.

OTHER STUDIES:
ECG shows sinus bradycardia.

attachments.title: Source clinical note
attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Found unresponsive on grass at outdoor music festival, brought in by EMS unarousable.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
According to her friends, she had been dancing and acting normally earlier in the day. They last saw her about 45 minutes prior to collapse and assumed she had gone to get food or water. When they found her, she was lying on her side and difficult to arouse. They deny seeing her consume alcohol but recall that she took several pills given to her by another attendee. A small pouch containing unlabeled tablets is found in her backpack.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
They are unaware of her taking any prescription medications and say she has no known medical history.

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
Her family history is non-contributory.

SOCIAL HISTORY:
She recently graduated from college and works as a part-time yoga instructor. There is no known history of psychiatric illness, and she has never expressed suicidal ideation. She does not smoke or drink regularly but has used recreational substances “occasionally” in the past, including marijuana and ecstasy.

VITAL SIGNS:
Her vital signs are notable for a pulse of 52/min, respiratory rate of 7/min, blood pressure of 108/64 mm Hg, oxygen saturation of 89% on room air, and temperature of 36.8°C (98.2°F).

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On arrival at the ED, the patient is unresponsive to sternal rub and moans only briefly to painful stimuli. She does not follow commands or open her eyes spontaneously. Pupils are 1 mm bilaterally and reactive to light. Skin is warm and dry, and there is no flushing, rash, cyanosis, or signs of trauma. There is no scleral icterus or needle marks. Neurologic exam shows decreased spontaneous movement but preserved deep tendon reflexes. There is no nystagmus.

OTHER STUDIES:
ECG shows sinus bradycardia with a normal QRS and QT interval.

PLAN:
The emergency medicine team prepares to intubate for airway protection.
